ranked_facts.concept_key: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum
ranked_facts.why: The finding of compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle is more likely to be associated with mechanical intestinal obstruction, specifically duodenal obstruction, rather than functional gastrointestinal disorders, inflammatory or infectious processes, or neoplastic processes.

A normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy is less likely to be associated with intrinsic luminal lesions, which are more commonly found in neoplastic processes or inflammatory/infectious processes, and is more consistent with extrinsic compression, such as that seen in vascular compression or mechanical obstruction.
